**Goal.** Turn yesterday's single fits into replicate evidence, and check whether the authors' bubble-plot / spatial check would actually catch a spatial truth. Then gather the theory (FWL, spatial confounding) and draft the discussion questions.

## Checklist

- [ ] Replicate stage 2 (200–500 per scenario) in `sim/replicate.R`; save .rds
- [ ] Moran's I on the iid intercepts under a spatial truth: detection rate
- [ ] Derivation: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell; skim Hodges & Reich (2010)
- [ ] Read Kéry & Kellner Ch. 18.5.2 and Ch. 18.8
- [ ] Draft discussion questions (including the cyclic spline in Q5)
- [ ] Stretch: rerun with 100 simulated locations

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("../sim/_load.R")
library(glmmTMB)
library(mgcv)
# NOTE: Moran's I needs spdep or ape; neither is installed in renv (see README).
```

## 1. Replicate stage 2

In `sim/replicate.R`: loop stage 2 for 200–500 replicates per scenario. Tabulate Treatment and DistReef estimates, SEs and coverage for each model.

**Done when:** one .rds per scenario in `results/`, and a summary table you'd put on a slide.

```{r}
#| label: replicate

```

## 2. Test the bubble-plot check

With a spatial truth, fit the iid model, run Moran's I on the 24 random intercepts, and record how often it detects the structure.

**Done when:** a detection rate per scenario (and ideally per ϕ).

```{r}
#| label: morans-i
# TODO: for each replicate, extract the 24 random intercepts from the iid fit.
# TODO: run Moran's I (spdep or ape) and record the detection rate.
```

## 3. Derivation → `notes/derivations.qmd`

Work through the Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem. Then skim Hodges & Reich (2010) on spatial confounding.

**Done when:** the Mon section of `notes/derivations.qmd` is filled in, and you can say in one line what FWL implies for DistReef here.

## 4. Reading

Kéry & Kellner, Ch. 18.5.2 (parametric bootstrap) and Ch. 18.8 (regularization).

**Done when:** one note on each, saying how it connects to the replicates or to the basis-function penalty.

## 5. Draft discussion questions

Include one on why the Q5 shoaling GAMM uses `s(DistReef, bs = "cc")` (a cyclic spline).

**Done when:** 4–6 questions per paper, in the decks' Discussion slides.
